name: Affordance Theory
axiom: An object's properties suggest what can be done with it, before any label says so.
trigger: A control that works looks exactly like the text around it, so nobody tries it.

checklist.text: Give every control a fill, border, or weight the surrounding text does not have.
Keep links underlined or coloured at rest; hover styling alone is not a signifier.
Draw a grip on anything draggable, and make the whole surface respond to the drag.
Watch first-time users try to click; every dead click marks an affordance that was not visible.

antiPattern.violation: Call-to-action buttons are set as plain text with no border, fill, or underline, identical to body copy.
antiPattern.remediation: Controls sit in filled rounded containers that contrast with the surface and lift on hover.

parametricParams.caption: EITHER SURFACE CAN SAY PRESS ME

academicOrigin.title: The Theory of Affordances
academicOrigin.publication: Perceiving, Acting, and Knowing (Shaw & Bransford, eds.)
